solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wisdom of rugby union devotee, initially blocking change?

indicators.note: to block something is to sit inside its path, so these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: change in the sense of coins, pennies
RU is the standard abbreviation for rugby union

indicators.note: initially points to only the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the first letter of devotee

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a rugby fan's sensible caution keeps them from adapting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like a verb meaning alteration, but here it is loose coins in a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is careful good judgement, a close synonym of practical wisdom.

clue.text: It's bound to be useful to those in need of a fix

definitions.text: It's bound to be useful to those in need of a fix

parts.words: It's bound to be useful to those in need of a fix
parts.note: surface reading: something certain to help addicts craving their next dose
setter's reading: bound means stitched between covers like a book, and a fix is a mending job on a machine

explanation.surface: Something is certain to help addicts desperate for their next dose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain', and 'fix' looks like a drug dose; read instead as a bound book for people mending something.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbook of instructions for mending a machine is a book, bound, that helps anyone carrying out a repair.

clue.text: Silent after moving sign up

indicators.note: once the letters have been moved around they no longer stand in their printed order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone quietly agrees to join after relocating.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to enrol, especially in the armed forces, which is to put your name down.

clue.text: Directs cattle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: guides or points in a direction
second meaning: young castrated bulls raised for beef

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a drover herding cattle; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for guiding a course and a plural noun for bullocks reared for meat.

clue.text: I'm thankful I left the last part!

parts.note: ta is an informal British way of saying thanks
taken as written
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone is relieved they walked out before the final section.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you, what you say when you are thankful.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail of anything is its end portion, the final bit to come.

clue.text: King and bishop visiting miserly comic character

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone else's home, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: mean means stingy
R is short for rex, Latin for king
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A monarch and a bishop call on a tight-fisted funny man.
explanation.walkthrough: R and B go inside MEAN. Mr Bean is the largely silent comic character played by Rowan Atkinson.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Bean is a famous fictional figure from British television comedy, so a comic character.

clue.text: One's got a large bill, we hear also prison

indicators.note: what we hear is speech, so the word is chosen by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: too means also, and is spelt differently here
the can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Someone facing a big debt may also face jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks financial, but it is a beak.
explanation.definitionFit: The toucan is a tropical bird famous for its enormous, brightly coloured beak.

clue.text: Fresh anvil seizure to make for everyone

indicators.note: something made fresh is newly put together, so these letters are reworked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's tool has been confiscated again, oddly for the benefit of everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To universalize something is to extend it so it applies to all people.

clue.text: One had, close to collapse, a brainwave

parts.note: I had is contracted to I'd, with one as I

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of collapse
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone close to breaking down suddenly had a bright thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever thought, which is an idea.

clue.text: Lie in bed, writhing: such awful food!

definitions.note: describes the food; the answer is the adjective for it

indicators.note: writhing is twisting about, so these letters are contorted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient groans in bed after a dreadful hospital meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: food so awful is unfit to eat, which is the adjective the grid wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Inedible means unfit to be eaten, which is what truly awful food is.

clue.text: University books with girl's stories

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
Ruth is a girl's name, here possessive

explanation.surface: A student's university texts sit beside a young woman's tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories in the sense of fibs or lies, which are falsehoods.

clue.text: Waste no time — once in hospital, that is

parts.note: H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Someone once admitted to hospital should not dawdle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' belongs to the definition, marking an archaic word; it is not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hie is an old word meaning hurry, so going without delay.

clue.text: Mediterranean island hotel based in the centre

indicators.note: the answer sits in the middle of the words that follow, straddling them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean island has a hotel located in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is an Italian island off Tuscany, where Napoleon was exiled.

clue.text: Bachelor: most slimy, and most drunken!

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA
most oozy, the most slimy and seeping

explanation.surface: A single man is judged the sleaziest and the drunkest of the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Boozy means fond of drink or drunk, so its superlative means most intoxicated.

clue.text: Chance meeting with a character abroad

parts.note: a bet is a chance or gamble
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lucky encounter with a person met on holiday overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a letter, and 'abroad' makes it a foreign alphabet's.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, a foreign written symbol.

clue.text: Lay-by for Americans and others, none parking on street

parts.note: the rest means the others
St is the abbreviation for street
O is the zero figure, meaning none
P is the road-sign symbol for parking

explanation.surface: A roadside stopping place for American drivers, where nobody is allowed to park on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the none-and-parking letters after the street ones. A lay-by is a British roadside pull-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Rest stop is the American term for a roadside area where drivers pull off to pause.

clue.text: Artist and attorney extremely reckless, we detect

definitions.note: the answer speaks as the detectors, a plural noun

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
DA is a US district attorney

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the two end letters of reckless

explanation.surface: A painter and a lawyer behave so rashly that we notice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the devices speaking: radars are what say 'we detect'.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar systems locate aircraft and ships by reflected radio waves, so they detect objects.

clue.text: Family in southern New York looking underfed?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other pieces that surround it

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
NY is the abbreviation for New York
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Relatives living in the south of New York appear to be going hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Southern New York' reads as one place, but it splits into two abbreviations that sandwich the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny means very thin, as someone who is underfed appears.

clue.text: Part of Mass some varied: sung avidly backwards!

indicators.note: read backwards means the letters run from right to left
some means only a portion of the following words is used

parts.note: the run of letters straddling these words, from the end of the first to the start of the last

explanation.surface: Part of a church service was sung differently, enthusiastically and in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters hide from the end of 'varied' to the start of 'avidly', read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: The Agnus Dei, Latin for Lamb of God, is a prayer section of the Roman Catholic Mass.

clue.text: Knowledge besetting Raskolnikov's heart leads to depression

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the name

explanation.surface: Learning surrounding Dostoevsky's anti-hero leads to gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Raskolnikov, the hero of Crime and Punishment, has eleven letters, so his heart is the sixth, L. GEN wraps around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, a hollow or depression in the land.

clue.text: Put down large assistance

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone dismissed a generous offer of help.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past tense of lay, to set something down.

clue.text: One giving out cards, but not giving away cars!

definitions.text: One giving out cards, but not giving away cars!

parts.note: first reading: the person who distributes playing cards round the table
setter's joke: the same title belongs to a car trader, who sells vehicles rather than handing them out

explanation.walkthrough: The card-game sense and the motor-trade sense share one word; the joke is that a motor trader charges for what a card distributor hands out free.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who distributes the cards in a game has the same title as a trader in vehicles.

clue.text: Man is upset about variable, brutal philosophy

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the other piece
something upset is knocked over and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
z is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A man is distressed by a fickle and cruel creed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nazism was the violent fascist ideology of Hitler's party, a brutal political doctrine.
